page: Microsoft Azure D8pds_v5 is an ARM-based general-purpose server instance powered by an 8-core Ampere Altra Neoverse-N1 processor running at 3.0 GHz. It features 8 dedicated physical cores with a single thread per core, 32.0 GB of system memory providing 4.0 GB per core, and a 307 GB local storage drive. The CPU architecture is arm64, utilizing the ARMv8 instruction set with a 32 MB L3 cache and hardware-accelerated AES cryptography, though it lacks x86-specific vector extensions like AVX or AMX.

Performance benchmarks place the D8pds_v5 in the average tier for multi-core operations, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 14512.61 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 5955.0. Memory performance is characterized by a high cached read bandwidth of 565.91 GB/sec, which drops to 68.42 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. Single-threaded tasks show some limitations, with Geekbench single-core scores falling into the weak category at 1055.0, and bzip3 single-threaded decompression rated as poor at 7.34 GB/sec. However, the instance maintains steady average performance in database operations and Redis SET operations, reaching 10.92 million operations per second.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the D8pds_v5 offers a balanced resource density of 4 GB of RAM per vCPU alongside dedicated physical cores, making it a viable option for workloads that benefit from ARM's power efficiency and consistent core performance without hyperthreading overhead. The inclusion of 307 GB of local storage and Premium Storage capability adds value for IO-sensitive tasks. This server is best suited for general-purpose workloads, static web serving, software compilation, and lightweight database or Redis caching layers.
description: The Microsoft Azure D8pds_v5 is an ARM-based general-purpose server instance featuring 8 dedicated physical cores powered by an Ampere Neoverse-N1 processor running at 3.0 GHz. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of RAM and 307 GB of local storage, with support for Premium Storage. Operating on the arm64 architecture, it delivers steady, average multi-core performance, as evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 5955.0 and a Redis throughput of 10.92 million SET operations per second. While single-threaded performance and vector-heavy operations are relatively weak due to the lack of AVX/AMX extensions, its high memory read bandwidth of 565.91 GB/sec (cached) and dedicated core allocation make it highly efficient for balanced workloads. It is well-suited for static web serving, software compilation, and database operations.
